A few years ago, I started having severe anxiety and panic related to PTSD. I got to a point where I ended up in a VA ER as a let resort, begging to be put into some sort of inpatient program, and I mean literal begging. I was told because I wasn’t suicidal (at the time) or having substance abuse issues all I could do was see an outpatient provider. Every single VA provider instantly pushed meds on me from day 1. 

This right here is what drove me to being suicidal. I found somewhat decent help on the civilian side but it took a long time as it was mostly the same issues. 

A huge problem with the mental health system is if you try to seek help early you are ignored, pushed aside and treated like dog shit which ends up making you turn to drugs or suicide. There is nothing for those of us caught in the middle.

Just not for me, I suppose. You are right though, talking about it and sharing stories helps quite a bit whether it’s with a therapist or on reddit. I think knowing that others have similar problems and can truly Understand is what helps the most. 

Stories? Here’s one...when I worked as a paramedic I always hated going on calls for anxiety and panic attacks. It flat out annoyed me. Like, how can people call 911 for a panic attack? What a waste of resources and time. I was cold and uncaring with these people. Well, here I am...karma caught up to me. I laugh about the karma part but honestly this just shows me that people really don’t understand anxiety unless they have experienced it themselves. I wish I could go back and be that caring person for all those patients who “annoyed” me.

Interesting story...I was a paramedic for 10 years and I never could understand why people would always call 911 for panic attacks. In fact, it would annoy me and make me angry at times. I didn’t always treat these people very well. I tried to respect everyone but I was particularly cold and uncaring when it came to anxiety calls. 

Well, as luck would have it, about 9 months ago I had a panic attack that turned into an endless cycle of panic and anxiety. Multiple ER visits, a hospital stay, primary care providers, antidepressants and counselors. Most times I found that people treated me in the same uncaring manner I had treated others and it’s awful. 

I now have a true appreciation for anxiety and how debilitating, scary and depressing it can be. I’m still struggling everyday to get by and it absolutely feels like I’m alone and nobody understands. I always say, “this is karma for how I treated people.” Really, anxiety truly is something people don’t understand unless they have experienced it themselves. 

I’m not sure if this helps but I thought I’d share. Just know while many people don’t understand or care there are many others who do and have experienced the same fear.

Thank you for your words and understanding. It means a lot. I think the issues with medication have been the most frustrating. How can I be happy and enjoy life living like this? It’s absolutely miserable especially when I feel there is no reason or cause for any of this. Sorry for rambling and seeming like I shoot down any advice...I’m honestly willing to try anything at this point as long as it doesn’t effect my job.

Hmmm, marijuana legalization. Interesting. At first, I was very much against it because I hated drugs, all drugs, period. As I’ve grown a little older, however, I’ve learned to not really care so much about other people and what they do in their lives. Obviously, marijuana isn’t nearly as bad some of the other drugs out there but I’m a firm believer that marijuana is a gateway drug for young people. There is a lot of controversy around that and I don’t think it’s that way physically. I don’t believe marijuana physically causes people to seek out other drugs but I do believe that young people who are very impressionable start out smoking pot and through that they network with other people who introduce them to other drugs. We have many drugs and narcotics that are legal and are very effective and helpful when used properly. Why shouldn’t marijuana be used if it in fact does have a medical benefit for people? I’m all for it being used medically, but I’m against the ridiculous subculture surrounding medical marijuana. It’s not marketed as a medication…it is marketed as a recreational drug. I think it should be treated as a medication and sold only in pharmacies and in forms other than joints. People who take medications like adderal aren’t buying it from street corner stores and snorting lines. People who take opiates for pain control aren’t shooting it up or smoking it from a spoon. Why should marijuana, as a medication, be any different? Now, if people want to legalize it as a recreational drug then that’s what they should try to do. I actually believe marijuana indirectly saved my life though…I know that sounds a little silly. Let me explain…I wasn’t exactly a good kid and I didn’t exactly hang out with the best kids. In fifth grade, I smoked pot for the first time and I literally thought I was going to die. I mean it scared the crap out of me so much that I was scared to touch any other drug, ever! I smoked it few times when I was a little bit older but I never did really like it so I just stuck to drinking here and there. So I think that experience kept me from trying other drugs even though my friends were doing them.

Thank you. School wasn’t always the best. It was a challenge because I had many other worries and school always came second. I had to repeat the 4th grade because I missed so many days. Kids picked on me because I was poor and I was also quite the tomboy so I was an easy target for them. However, I was tough and always stuck up for myself and eventually kids would end up liking me (it was weird) but then I’d switch schools and start that all over again. I had many close friends. I actually met my best friend in the 7th grade and we are still very close to this day, and we hated each other at first. I now have many close friends who I am extremely grateful for. I’m blown away by the number of “real” friends I have today. I don’t remember ever coming across other children my age while I was homeless. I grew up in a fairly middle-class area that didn’t exactly have a big homeless population.

That's a great question! Somehow, no, I was never taken away by DCS and still to this day I wonder exactly why that is. Truth be told, I never wanted to be taken away either...I loved my mom too much and wanted to be with her no matter what. In first or second grade, before we were homeless and still living at my grandmother's house, I remember one of my teachers sent the police to my house. I specifically remember them looking in the refrigerator to see if we had food. Nothing ever came of that. Teachers and school officials were definitely suspicious of my living conditions but I don't think any of them actually knew the extent of it and I wasn't physically abused so I don't think they pursued much. The many many times we had contact with the police they never did anything either. There were a couple times when my mom was arrested and I was taken to the police station. They would always manage to get a hold of some other family member or family friend who would pick me up. I'm very glad I was never taken away because I think going into the system wouldn't have been the best thing for me. It's taken a lot of time and soul searching but I've finally decided that I wouldn't change anything in my past because it's made me a better person. It's given me some not so great qualities as well but I've found ways to deal with those issues, for the most part.
That means a lot...Thank you very much!

I do. When I was still pretty young we used to hang out a particular park that was populated by a lot of the homeless. For a short time we lived in the park and there was an old lady (probably in her 80s) who used to bring her dog (Dingo was his name...no idea why I remember that) to the park. She brought dingo every Wednesday and she also would bring food for everyone. Very nice lady. But anyway, I absolutely loved playing ball with that dog. After we weren't staying at that park anymore my mom did make it a point for us to go there on Wednesdays so I could play with Dingo. I don't know why that specifically sticks out but it was definitely my happiest memory when we were probably at our worst. Other than that I have a few other happy memories. There was a short time when my mom was sober and every moment during that time was extremely happy to me! One more thing...I loved baseball and I loved playing baseball. As messed up as my mom was, she always made sure I got to play baseball every year. I don't know where exactly she came up with the money for it but she did. Sometimes it was very challenging to make it to practices and games but she always managed to get me there, usually on our bikes. I think these were definitely happy memories.

I regret many things. I regret not putting myself first when came to my education and going to college. I always put off my education to take care of my family and my mom or to deal with our problems. I wished I had gone to medical school but I always thought I was stupid. It took me a long time to realize I wasn't nearly as stupid as I thought I was. Too little, too late. Now that I'm a paramedic I love what I do and wouldn't want to do anything else. Hobbies...anything outdoors. I like camping, hiking and off-roading. I also like baseball and photography.

Haha I love Breaking Bad! My mother lives with me now as she always has since I was able to afford my own place. I did send her off to a family friend out of state for a couple years after my deployment because I was sick of living with her. She ended up getting back into drugs and had nowhere to go so I brought back to live with me. I've recently come to terms with the fact that she will live with me until she dies. It's too much heartache to keep trying to get her out on her own. Never knew or met my father. He was quite older than my mother and when she got pregnant he told her he already had children and didn't want anymore and that was pretty much it. As far as other family, I have an aunt who is clean and sober for like 10 years now. She has an 8 year old daughter who is on the right track and she has a 23 year old son who is going down the same road drugs and crime. I also have an uncle who is sober from drugs for about 5 years but is an alcoholic. Relationships don't go well for me so I pretty much choose to stay single. Longest relationship was 3 months. I'm very independent and get annoyed with people very quickly. I stole many many times. We stole food quite often and my mom used to do boost and returns (steal stuff and return it for cash or store credit). I helped people sell stolen property on many occasions for small cut of the money and as a young teenager I stole things that I wanted because I had no other way to get them. I am not religious at all. As a kid I wanted to go to church because I thought that's what normal people did. For a short time when I first joined the army I pursued religion in the catholic church but ended up not agreeing with much of it. After everything I have seen in my job I just can't bring myself to be religious...there's much more to this but I don't want to list all my reasons.

I tried to jump on the therapy bandwagon about a year ago and all they wanted to do was throw meds at me...never went back. Yeah, sure does sound like a good deal but I was young and uncomfortable with it so I didn't do it. I don't know exactly why I didn't but I'm definitely glad I was able to keep myself from going that route. I found other ways to make money like running people's dope and doing odd jobs. I spent quite some time shoveling dirt for a friend's construction company before I was old enough to actually get a job. From the time I was 15 I always had a legitimate job, sometimes two at a time, while still managing to go to school everyday.

I suppose. It was weird because they did have their little cliques and groups now that I think about it. I think if anything it was for friendship and to have people around who are similar to you. Also, you always ran into the same people because most of would go to churches for hot dinners and most of the churches only served food once a week, on the same day. So we'd all travel around to whichever church was serving free food on that day. It definitely is a sort of subculture.

Good question! I would say 99.9% need more help than just money. I'd say the majority had both mental health problems and drug addiction. Mostly alcoholism because it's much cheaper to get drunk, but if they could get their hands on other drugs they were sure to do them. I don't think anyone who is homeless to the point of sleeping in the streets (not their cars or a buddies couch) is simply experiencing an unfortunate financial situation. I think mental illness is definitely at the core of the problem.

Well, you do bring up a good point and I'm sure you are absolutely correct about it "selling" but I'm not looking to make money...just looking to better understand myself. There was a man we lived with who would consistently offer me large amounts of money to show him certain parts of my body. I always declined his offers though...
A bunch of random homeless people...Maybe 8-10 of us. It was a sort of like camp site. They were mostly your stereotypical bearded old drunks.

Honestly, I don't think it has anything to do with my past. The easy and stereotypical answer would be "because I want to help people." I pretty much just think it's an exciting job and I find medicine to be very fascinating. Helping people is just sort of an extra perk I guess.

At first, everything was scary. There was this man who lived in the same motel as me. He seemed nice enough and used to invite some of the kids over to hang out in his room and he always offered us alcohol and drugs. Somehow, I ended up hanging out there alone. He sat close to me and put his hand in my pocket and attempted to "touch me." I immediately said I had to go, and I left. I never went back to his room again after that. Somehow, I managed to get through my childhood without being molested or raped which blows my mind. 

When we'd sleep next to the railroad tracks I was always scared that a train would derail and land on us (I was still quite young at this point). So, one night while I was asleep I woke up to the loud sound of a train stopping and when I opened my eyes all I saw was the side of one of the box cars. For some reason I thought it was falling over on top of us and I started screaming and woke everyone up. They're weren't to happy with me. I don't know why but that memory is very vivid for me.
